findings.summary: The post-hoc account confuses four memory tasks with five learning sessions and understates Codex saves.

evidence.summary: RESULT calls these four learning sessions per cell, with Claude 2 OAW / 1 host / 1 unsaved and Codex only 1 saved. There are five: explicit s1, passing s1, superseded s1 and s2, handoff s1. Claude has 2 OAW saves, 2 host saves, 1 unsaved; Codex has 2 successful OAW/pending saves and 3 unsaved.

Codex superseded s2 item_16 successfully executes memory add, exit 0, with both replacement facts; s1 has no add. Thus M1 is correctly absent at the task level, but this is a real second save at the session level. Claude superseded has successful host-note writes in both s1 and s2; its old-body save also omits the required trailing period.

findings.fix: Distinguish task-level M1 (Claude 2/4, Codex 1/4) from five learning sessions per cell. Report the session counts above and describe the first Claude host save as incomplete for the exact old body.

findings.summary: Post-hoc interpretation softens failures and makes unsupported claims about noise, causation, and benefits that reverting would remove.

evidence.summary: The old-O and new-O small-change failure counts are both 2/8, on different units, and their totals are correctly reported. This does not establish that the threshold cannot distinguish effects, or that it mainly measures single-answer variation. There is only one old-O and one new-O counted answer per unit, across time, with several changes bundled.

The heading attributes a saving direction to R2, and the closing paragraph states that reverting R2 will remove savings and reverting M1+M2 will remove Claude gains. The data establish observed token/score differences, not their cause or outcomes after a revert. Native superseded recall differing across N1/N2 supports only the possibility of variation. The report itself concedes that changes cannot be assigned to one fix.

All adverse measurements are listed, but the phrase that R2 itself had no failed condition downplays the design-cost condition missed by Codex design-1-c1 (917116 to 1121239, +22.257%). This miss is report-only for disposition; it still is not evidence of a saving on that unit.

findings.fix: Keep the explicit post-hoc separation, but describe measured associations only: 2/8 failures in each version, three design-unit decreases and one increase, and changed recall counts. Say noise and fix effects cannot be separated. Remove predictions that reverting will remove benefits, and explicitly call the individual design-cost condition unmet without changing the preregistered disposition.

findings.summary: The stated disposition omits the mandatory final-commit gate, six-cell CI, and synchronized documentation after reverts.

evidence.summary: Both B memory thresholds and two A thresholds fail. Applying the concurrent rows correctly yields reverting M1+M2+R2, retaining M3/R1, and no M3/R1 or non-design-C blocker from these data. The per-design no-saving report remains applicable despite the eventual R2 revert.

The applicable final disposition row requires the final commit to rerun the gate and six-cell CI with documents synchronized. RESULT gives only a generic statement that numeric thresholds do not replace CI/release review; it does not state this concrete required follow-through. This is an omission, not evidence that CI was run or failed.

findings.fix: Append the mandatory final-commit gate, six-cell CI, and documentation synchronization to the disposition; distinguish required follow-up from completed work.

findings.summary: The preregistered design-only token aggregates are not reported.

evidence.summary: The design-cost rule requires both individual comparisons and an aggregate. RESULT supplies four individual design comparisons, C-class totals (including non-design large tasks), and whole-batch totals, but no design-only aggregate.
Recomputed design totals: Claude old 7720010 to new 2667668; Codex old 2820294 to new 2010971; combined old 10540304 to new 4678639. These totals do not negate the Codex design-1-c1 increase.

findings.fix: Add the design-only old/new subtotals for both cells, preserving the individual +22% counterexample.
